purpose: Research anchors for learning mechanisms used by the capability. These sources support mechanisms, not a guarantee that every learner or schedule will produce the same result.

sources.title: Test-enhanced learning: taking memory tests improves long-term retention
sources.product_implication: Prefer learner retrieval attempts before merely restudying or revealing answers when appropriate.

sources.title: Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis
sources.product_implication: Use spaced review, but do not present one fixed interval schedule as universally optimal.

sources.title: Learning concepts and categories: is spacing the enemy of induction?
sources.product_implication: Use interleaving selectively when learners must discriminate neighboring concepts; do not apply it mechanically to every task.

sources.title: The Distributed Practice Effect on Classroom Learning: A Meta-Analytic Review of Applied Research
sources.product_implication: Spacing has applied classroom evidence, but implementation should still adapt to subject, learner and retention horizon.

unsupported_shortcuts: Receiving a summary is not evidence of mastery.
Seeing an answer is not evidence of retrieval.
A fixed 1/7/30-day schedule is not universally optimal.
The Feynman label does not by itself prove learning; the useful mechanism is learner-generated explanation plus correction.
